panel_name: Reward and Novelty Mechanism Calibration Panel
purpose: Calibrate dopaminergic reward mechanisms related to environmental novelty and approach behavior. Understanding why novel architecture initially attracts and why the effect wanes is critical for designing spaces that maintain long-term engagement.

target_templates.name: Dopaminergic Novelty Reward
target_templates.mechanism: Environmental novelty → VTA dopamine release → NAcc approach behavior → reward learning → habituation over time
target_templates.architectural_relevance: Museums, retail, workplaces, educational facilities. Understanding the novelty-habituation curve helps design spaces that maintain engagement vs. spaces optimized for initial 'wow' that fades.

constructs_to_calibrate.name: novelty_response_peak
constructs_to_calibrate.description: Time to peak dopamine response after novelty exposure
constructs_to_calibrate.current_status: animal models well-characterized, human fMRI indirect

constructs_to_calibrate.name: habituation_time_constant
constructs_to_calibrate.description: Time for novelty response to decay to 50%

constructs_to_calibrate.name: optimal_novelty_level
constructs_to_calibrate.description: Intermediate novelty that maximizes approach without anxiety

constructs_to_calibrate.name: architectural_novelty_features
constructs_to_calibrate.description: Features that drive architectural novelty perception

constructs_to_calibrate.name: novelty_seeking_individual_differences
constructs_to_calibrate.description: Range of novelty preferences in population
constructs_to_calibrate.current_status: BIS/BAS scales validated but not applied to architecture

key_papers.contribution: fMRI showing SN/VTA activation to novel stimuli. Establishes neural basis for novelty-dopamine link.
Anticipation of novelty activates reward circuits. Shows novelty-seeking is intrinsically rewarding.
Arousal potential and the inverted-U relationship between complexity/novelty and preference.
Neural correlates of architectural judgment. Approach/avoidance decisions in architectural contexts.

design_features: Balance of familiar and novel elements
population_sensitivity: High novelty-seekers prefer more complex environments
Low novelty-seekers prefer predictable, familiar spaces
Age affects novelty tolerance (children vs. elderly)
Anxiety-prone individuals may find excessive novelty aversive

pre_reading: Understand dopamine circuit anatomy (VTA, NAcc, PFC)
calibration_protocol: 1. Define architectural novelty index (visual complexity, spatial unexpectedness, material variety)
2. Map novelty index to approach behavior probability
3. Model habituation curve for repeated exposure
5. Create WIS conversion from novelty-reward parameters
output_deliverables: Updated T17 template JSON with calibrated parameters
